title: Reciprocal translocation t(15;17)
clinical_history: A 34-year-old woman presents with bruising, pancytopenia, and laboratory evidence of disseminated intravascular coagulation. Bone marrow is packed with abnormal promyelocytes. Cancer cytogenetics is requested.
plain_language_interpretation: A female karyotype with 46 chromosomes and a reciprocal translocation between 15q and 17q. Breakpoints are written here as q24 and q21 (PML::RARA). Older maps used 15q22; that historical form is accepted as a variant in this exercise.
explanation: The t(15;17) translocation fuses PML with RARA and defines acute promyelocytic leukemia. It is a medical emergency because of coagulopathy; identification of the rearrangement (or PML::RARA) directs ATRA-based therapy. ISCN 2020 maps the 15q breakpoint to 15q24.1 rather than the older 15q22. This laboratory accepts both the contemporary t(15;17)(q24;q21) form and the historical q22;q21 form.
hints: This is an acquired myeloid neoplasm, not a constitutional syndrome of childhood.
The rearrangement involves chromosomes 15 and 17, both q-arm breakpoints.
Write a reciprocal translocation as t(15;17) followed by the breakpoint bands in the same order as the chromosomes.
